themes.name: Curricular Integration of ESD
themes.definition: The process of incorporating education for sustainable development into existing or new curricula in higher education institutions, often through program plans, modules, or specific courses.
evidence: [PauAss_2022] integrating sustainability into engineering or fundamental study programs (SPs)
[BomBui_2025] integrating sustainable development into courses and degree programs
[AcoEdu_2022] inclusion of the subject of education for sustainable development (ESD) in the undergraduate study plan

themes.name: Development of Sustainability Competences
themes.definition: Fostering specific skills, knowledge, and attitudes necessary for addressing sustainability challenges, including global competence, green skills, and problem-solving abilities.
evidence: [RisCom_2020] competences for solving complex problems
[KjeEdu_2021] holistic global competence development
[GarStr_2025] green skills and sustainable entrepreneurial intentions

themes.name: Transformative and Experiential Learning Approaches
themes.definition: Pedagogical methods that involve active engagement, real-world problems, and personal transformation to enhance sustainability education, such as project-based learning, design thinking, and game design.
evidence: [CotEdu_2019] transformative learning experience
[MacNur_2024] transformative learning using design thinking
[AriBri_2023] Project-Based Learning in renewable and sustainable energies

themes.name: Collaborative and Transdisciplinary Methods
themes.definition: Approaches that involve cooperation between universities and non-university partners, or across disciplines, to address sustainability issues through partnerships, networks, and collective engagement.
evidence: [HoiCre_2021] cooperation of universities and non-university partners
[GueCli_2025] international research consortium
[AdeEco_2021] Collaborative Online International Learning

themes.name: Assessment and Evaluation of ESD
themes.definition: The use of tools and methods to measure sustainability literacy, competences, or the effectiveness of ESD initiatives, including tests, surveys, and mapping tools.
evidence: [AikPro_2023] assessment through sustainability literacy test
[DécFos_2021] estimate the advancement of students’ knowledge and understanding
[AheEdu_2023] evaluation results

themes.name: Digital and Online Learning for ESD
themes.definition: The application of e-learning, MOOCs, and online platforms to deliver and enhance education for sustainable development, often through virtual seminars, research-based learning, or open online tools.
evidence: [HueSus_2022] E-Learning mechanisms and SDG coverage in MOOCs
[AheEdu_2023] research-based learning in an online environment
[de The_2017] European Virtual Seminar on Sustainable Development

themes.name: Challenges in Implementing ESD
themes.definition: Identified barriers or difficulties in integrating sustainability education into higher education, such as institutional constraints, lack of resources, stakeholder dynamics, or translating knowledge into action.
evidence: [O'NCha_2024] challenges of adding new themes to existing courses
[Al-The_2025] inappropriate distribution of power, legitimacy and urgency amongst the salient stakeholders
[HijCli_2025] students still face challenges translating their understanding of climate change science into action

data.meta_observations: Many abstracts focus on practical implementations and case studies, with prevalent methodologies like action research, surveys, and qualitative analysis. There is a strong emphasis on competences development and transformative learning, often linked to real-world applications and stakeholder engagement.
data.grounding_notes: All evidence is verbatim from the provided abstracts, adhering to anti-hallucination rules. Some abstracts have quality notes indicating missing elements (e.g., missing_results, no_quantitative_data), so inferences were avoided. Themes are derived inductively from observed terminology and patterns.
